Delhi, the 30th June, 2026
F. No. JC/EV/TPT/2026/02/281— Whereas, the Council of Ministers approved the Delhi Electric Vehicles
Policy 2026 vide Cabinet Decision No.3349 dated 29.06.2026.XXX
Now, therefore, in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (3) of section 67, read with clause (41) of
section 2 and other enabling provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and the rules made thereunder, the Lieutenant
Governor of the National Capital Territory of Delhi hereby notifies the Delhi Electric Vehicles Policy, 2026 with effect
from 01.07.2026.XXX

DELHI ELECTRIC VEHICLES POLICY, 2026

1. Introduction
1.1 Delhi is committed to curb air pollution and accordingly aims to promote and adopt clean mobility transition through
targeted incentives, infrastructure development, and strong regulatory measures. The Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy
2026– 2030 (four years) builds on this momentum to accelerate electric vehicle (EV) adoption, improve air quality, and
create a supportive ecosystem for electric mobility. The policy will be applicable from the date of the notification.
1.2 The policy draws its inspiration and support from Article 21 of the Constitution of India providing for right to life
which construes right to clean air and pollution free environment. Hon’ble Supreme Court in M.C. Mehta Vs. Union of
India and Ors has asked to review and revise respective electric vehicle (EV) policies. The policy also draws support
from various provisions of the Environment Protection Act 1986, Motor Vehicle (MV) Act 1988, especially Section
67(3) of MV Act 1988, which empowers the State Government notwithstanding anything contain in MV Act 1988, to
make schemes for the transportation of goods and passengers for the promotion of development and efficiency in
transportation for various causes including last-mile connectivity, improving urban transport, the protection and
enhancement of the environment, promotion of energy conservation, improvement of the quality of life etc.
1.3 The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), in its latest report ‘Id entification of the causes for
worsening AQI in Delhi NCR’1 submitted to Hon’ble Supreme Court, has identified vehicular emissions as the largest
contributor (23% during winter) to air pollution in the National Capital Territory of Delhi. Two-wheelers constitute
approximately 67% of the total vehicle stock in Delhi, making their rapid electrification critical for achieving
meaningful reductions in vehicular emissions. Further, three-wheelers, commercial cars, and N1 category goods vehicles
exhibit high daily utilisation and mileage, resulting in a disproportionate contribution to urban air pollution.
Accordingly, prioritised electrification of these vehicle segments is essential to achieve sustained improvements in air
quality in Delhi.
1.4 This policy emphasises EV incentives, scalable charging infrastructure, clear electrification mandates, and
development of supporting systems such as battery recycling and disposal.
2. Policy Objectives
▪ Accelerate adoption of EVs across all major vehicle segments
▪ Support installation of a comprehensive public and private charging network across Delhi
▪ Enable a robust EV supply chain including battery recycling, servicing, and component recovery
▪ Improve air quality by reducing reliance on Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles
▪ Ensure fiscal efficiency and transparent implementation
3. Definitions
3.1 Electric Vehicle shall mean "Battery Operated Vehicle" means a vehicle adapted for use upon roads and powered
exclusively by an electric motor whose traction energy is supplied exclusively by traction battery installed in the
vehicle.2
3.2 Operational Guidelines shall mean separate detailed instructions issued by GNCTD from time to time for
implementation, eligibility verification, and disbursal procedures under this Policy.

3.3 Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment (EVSE) shall mean an element in Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure
(EVCI) that supplies electrical energy for recharging the battery of electric vehicles.3
3.4 Public Charging Station (PCS) shall mean an EV charging station where any electric vehicle can get its battery
recharged.4
3.5 Community Charging Station means semi-public charging station installed at Group Housing Societies or other
residential accommodations where only residents or authorized visitors can get their EV charged.5
3.6 Battery Swapping Station (BSS) shall mean a station where any electric vehicle can get its discharged battery or
partially charged battery replaced by a charged battery.6
3.7 Definitions 3.1 to3.6 shall stand updated as per modifications made by the concerned authorities from time to time.
4. Financial Incentives
4.1 Purchase Incentive
4.1.1 All purchase incentive under this policy shall be disbursed through direct benefit transfer to individual buyer/
proprietary firms/ agencies/ companies being residents of NCT of Delhi and the vehicle being purchased and registered
in Delhi. Eligible beneficiaries shall apply directly for subsidy claims through a mechanism notified by the Transport
Department, GNCTD.
4.1.2 A Model Approval Committee constituted under the Transport Department shall be responsible for empanelment
of EV models across eligible vehicle segments for availing incentives and subsidies under the Policy. The Committee
shall examine and approve vehicle models based on the eligibility criteria, technical specifications, and other conditions
prescribed under the operational guidelines. Only models approved and empanelled by the Committee shall be eligible
for purchase incentives under the Policy.
4.1.3 The application for purchase incentive shall be submitted within 30 days from the date of generation of the
Registration Certificate (RC). The eligible subsidy amount shall be disbursed within 60 days from the date of submission
of the application on the digital portal, subject to verification and fulfilment of applicable requirements.
4.1.4 Any vehicle availing purchase incentive under the Delhi EV Policy, 2026 shall not be eligible for issuance of a
No Objection Certificate (NoC) for transfer or re-registration in another State/UT for a period of three years from the
date of notification of the policy.
4.2 Two-Wheelers
4.2.1 Eligibility: The ex-showroom price of the electric two-wheeler shall not exceed INR 2.25 lakh.

4.2.2 Incentive Structure (Year-wise Registration): GNCTD shall provide the following incentive to promote
electric two-wheeler adoption in the NCT of Delhi:

*Incentive shall be applicable to both plug-in and battery swapping e-two-wheelers models.

auto adoption in NCT of Delhi:

4.5 The eligibility of EV models for purchase incentives shall be aligned to FAME 2, PM E-DRIVE scheme, and other
schemes/guidelines of Government of India or GNCTD, if any.
4.6 Scrapping Incentives
4.6.1 Electric Two-Wheeler: A scrapping incentive of ₹10,000 shall be provided upon purc hase of a new electric vehicle
under this policy, provided the purchase is made within six (6) months of issuance of the Certificate of Deposit (CoD)
from an authorised scrapping facility. This incentive shall be applicable for scrapping of Delhi registered BS-IV and
below, two-wheelers.
4.6.2 Electric Three-Wheeler (L5M): A scrapping incentive of ₹25,000 shall be provided upon purchase of a new electric
vehicle under this policy, provided the purchase is made within six (6) months of issuance of the Certificate of Deposit
(CoD) from an authorised scrapping facility. This incentive shall be applicable for scrapping of Delhi registered BS-IV
and below, three-wheelers (L5M).
4.6.3Electric Car (Non-Transport):A scrapping incentive of ₹1,00,000 shall be provided upon purchase of a new
electric car under this policy, subject to an ex-showroom price not exceeding ₹30 lakh , provided the purchase is made
within six (6) months of issuance of the Certificate of Deposit (CoD) from an authorised scrapping facility. This
incentive shall be applicable for the scrapping of Delhi-registered BS-IV and below carsand shall belimited to the
first 1,00,000 eligible applicants under this policy.
4.6.4Electric Four-Wheeler Goods Carriers (N1 Trucks):A scrapping incentive of ₹50,000 shall be provided upon
purchase of a new electric vehicle under this policy, provided the purchase is made within six (6) months of issuance of
the Certificate of Deposit (CoD) from an authorised scrapping facility. This incentive shall be applicable for scrapping
of Delhi registered BS-IV and below, four-wheeler Goods Carriers (N1 Trucks).
4.6.5 A scrapping incentive of ₹15,000 shall be provided upo n scrapping of a Gramin Sewa vehicle registered in Delhi,
subject to the condition that a new electric Gramin Sewa vehicle (D+6/D+7) equipped with a Li-ion battery or any other
advanced/progressive battery technology is purchased within six months from the date of issuance of the Certificate of
Deposit (CoD) by an authorised scrapping facility.
4.6.6 All scrapping incentive shall be disbursed through direct benefit transfer to individual buyer/ proprietary
firms/ agencies/ companies being residents of NCT of Delhi and the vehicle being registered in Delhi. Eligible
beneficiaries shall apply directly for subsidy claims through a mechanism notified by the Transport Department,
GNCTD.
4.6.7 All scrapping incentive on CoD shall be applicable only to the owner of the scrapped vehicle.
4.7 Road Tax, Registration Fee Exemption and No Entry Exemption
4.7.1 All electric vehicles (subject to clause 4.7.2, and 4.7.3) purchased and registered in the NCT of Delhi during the
policy period shall be granted 100% exemption from road tax throughout the life of the vehicle and registration fees at
the time of vehicle registration.
4.7.2 All electric cars with ex-showroom price below or equal to 30 lakhs purchased and registered in the NCT of Delhi
shall be granted 100% exemption from road tax and registration fees till 31 March 2030.
4.7.3 All electric cars with ex-showroom price above 30 lakhs purchased and registered in the NCT of Delhi shall not
be granted any exemption from road tax and registration fees.

4.7.4 No Entry Exemption for N2 E-Trucks: The first one thousand (1,000) private electric trucks falling under the N2
vehicle category (not being used for any purpose in departments/autonomous bodies/corporations/boards and similar
institutions under GNCTD including Municipal Corporation of Delhi, New Delhi Municipal Council and Delhi
Cantonment Board) and purchased and registered in Delhi within three (3) months from the date of notification of this
Policy shall be exempted from the prohibition of no-entry timing for 10 years from the date of registration of the vehicle.
The details regarding this provision shall be given in the operational guidelines.
5. Charging and Battery Swapping Infrastructure Development

5.1 GNCTD shall send proposal under PM E-Drive scheme of the Ministry of Heavy Industry, Government of India or
any other schemes of Government of India for availing support for charging and battery swapping infrastructure and
will also allocate sufficient funds to Power Department to augment the public & community charging and battery
swapping infrastructure.
5.2 Delhi Transco Limited (DTL) shall act as the nodal agency for planning, coordination, and implementation of public
electric vehicle charging and battery swapping infrastructure in the NCT of Delhi.
5.3 DTL shall aggregate demand, proposed locations, and load requirements for public EV charging and battery
swapping infrastructure across departments and agencies, and shall undertake system-level planning to ensure optimal
siting, grid readiness, and phased deployment.
5.4 DTL shall develop, notify, and periodically update Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs) detailing technical
standards, approval processes, timelines, service level benchmarks, and monitoring mechanisms for the deployment and
operation of public EV charging and swapping infrastructure.
5.5 DTL shall develop, operate, or integrate a dedicated digital portal—either under the PM E-DRIVE framework or a
GNCTD-specific platform—for end-to-end management of public EV charging and battery swapping infrastructure,
including site onboarding, approvals, monitoring, and reporting, in coordination with District Magistrates (DMs),
Deputy Commissioners (DCs) through revenue department, and other concerned agencies.
5.6 In addition to DTL; DISCOMs, private entities, real estate developers, and other eligible stakeholders shall be
encouraged to establish public EV charging stations across the NCT of Delhi.
5.7A High-Powered Committee shall be constituted under the Chairpersonship of the Chief Secretary, GNCTD,
comprising representatives from the Departments of Transport, Power, Planning, Environment, Finance, Delhi Transco
Limited (DTL), DISCOMs, and any other department/agency/body as deemed necessary.
5.8 The composition of the Committee along with ToR shall be notified separately with approval of the Hon’ble Chief
Minister.
5.9 Single Window Clearance: DTL shall create a single window facility for charge point and battery swapping operators
to enable faster clearance and procuring expedited EV connection to deploy public and semi-public charging stations in
NCT of Delhi.
5.10 Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs), Group Housing Societies, residential communities and private entities
shall be encouraged to facilitate the deployment of community/private EV charging infrastructure within residential
premises and other private spaces to support convenient and accessible charging for public.
5.11 DISCOMs shall be encouraged to explore the deployment of Energy Storage Systems (ESS) at e-bus depots to
support load management, reduce peak demand, and enhance grid reliability. Further, DISCOMs through DERC may
also explore suitable Time-of-Day (ToD) tariff structures and differential electricity pricing mechanisms to reduce EV
charging costs, enable efficient charging behaviour, and improve overall grid efficiency.
5.12 To support the adoption of electric trucks and electric buses, adequate charging infrastructure shall be developed
at suitable government-owned locations. This will enable reliable charging access and encourage greater participation
of private fleet operators in the transition to electric mobility.
6. Role of OEMs
6.1Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) shall ensure adequate and timely supply of electric vehicles across all
eligible segments during the policy period.
6.2All OEMs operating in the National Capital Territory of Delhi shall ensure the deployment of at least one public
electric vehicle charging station per dealer comprising a minimum of three (3) charging points for two-/three-wheelers
and two (2) charging points for four-wheelers. The location of such charging stations shall, to the extent feasible, be
aligned with the siting categories and locations specified under Category A, B, and C of the OPERATIONAL
GUIDELINES FOR DEPLOYMENT OF EV PUBLIC CHARGING STATIONS (EV PCS) UNDER THE PM E-
DRIVE SCHEME.

6.3 The OEMs shall aim to stabilise the cost of EVs to make it affordable for the residents of NCT of Delhi.
7. Additional Ecosystem Development Measures
7.1 Battery Recycling
7.1.1 The Environment Department shall ensure strict adherence by Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and
other obligated entities to all applicable provisions of the BATTERY WASTE MANAGEMENT RULES, 2022, as
amended from time to time, including requirements related to Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), reporting, and
environmentally sound management of waste batteries.
7.1.2 The Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) shall, through an appropriate policy framework, facilitate the
deployment of battery collection centres across the National Capital Territory of Delhi under a Public-Private
Partnership (PPP) model, in collaboration with authorised recyclers and other eligible entities, to enable convenient,
accessible, and environmentally sound collection of waste batteries.
7.1.3 DPCC shall notify Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and
other obligated entities to ensure the safe collection, storage, transportation, and transfer of waste batteries to authorised
recyclers or Producer Responsibility Organisations (PROs), in compliance with applicable environmental regulations,
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements, and safety standards. OEMs shall submit periodic reports on
EPR target compliance and battery traceability to the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), in the prescribed
format and frequency by DPCC.
7.1.4 The Government of NCT of Delhi shall promote a battery traceability-enabled ecosystem, based on unique
battery identifiers, to support battery refurbishment, safe second-life use, and environmentally sound recycling.
8. Electrification Mandates for Registration
8.1 Electric Three-Wheelers (L5) and N1 Goods Carrier
8.1.1 From 01 January 2027, only electric three-wheelers (L5) shall be permitted for new registration in the NCT of
Delhi.
8.1.2 From 01 January 2027, only electric N1 goods carriers shall be permitted for new registration in the NCT of Delhi
8.2 Electric Two-Wheelers
8.2.1 From 01 April 2028, only electric two-wheelers shall be permitted for new registration in the NCT of Delhi.
8.3 Electric Four-Wheelers
8.3.1 The GNCTD intends to bring out electrification mandates for four-wheelers in future as well as aim to make a
framework for disincentivising polluting vehicles that use inefficient fuels.
8.4 School Buses
8.4.1All schools in NCT of Delhi shall adhere to the electrification targets as stated in the table below:
Effective Date Minimum Electric Share of Fleet
Till completion of year 2 from the date of notification 10%
Till completion of year 3 from the date of notification 20%
Till 31st March 2030 30%

8.4.2 The mandate shall apply to the total school bus fleet, whether owned, leased or hired. The Education Department,
GNCTD, shall ensure adherence to the abovementioned mandate.
8.4.3 Effort will be made to encourage concessionaires of DTC/Cluster e-buses to provide facility in depots for charging
of school buses as per mutually agreed terms and conditions decided with Transport Department/DTC. Further, funds
shall be sought under PM E-DRIVE scheme and other sources for providing adequate charging infrastructure in this
regard.
8.5 Fleet Aggregators operating in NCT of Delhi
8.5.1 Electrification mandates for fleet aggregators and delivery service providers are as follows:- No conventional ICE
vehicles running purely on diesel or petrol shall be inducted in the existing fleet of 4-Wheeler LCVs, 4-Wheeler LGVs
(N1 category up to 3.5 Ton) and 2-Wheelers with effect from 01.01.2026 provided Induction of BS-VI emission standard
2-Wheelers shall be permitted in the existing fleet up to 31.12.2026.

8.5.2 All other provisions of the existing Delhi Motor Vehicle Aggregator and Delivery Service Provider Scheme (2023)
shall remain unchanged and shall apply. Aggregators and Delivery Service Providers shall be encouraged for transition
of their fleets to electric vehicles in order to support the adoption of clean mobility solutions and reduce vehicular
emissions in the NCT of Delhi.
8.6 Government Fleet
8.6.1 All hired/leased,non-transport and light passenger vehicles in GNCTD from the date of notification of this policy
shall,to the extent possible, be electric.
8.6.2 All new intra-state buses to be inducted by the Delhi Transport Corporation and the Transport Department,
GNCTD on its own, from the date of notification of this policy, shall be electric.
8.6.3 All N1/N2/N3 trucks and M2/M3 passenger vehicles purchased/leased/hired bydepartments/autonomous
bodies/corporations/boards and similar institutions under GNCTD including Municipal Corporation of Delhi, New
Delhi Municipal Council and Delhi Cantonment Board, from the date of notification of this policy, shall be only electric.
8.7 If cleaner fuel vehicles are introduced during the period of this policy, such as hydrogen fuel, the same may be
inducted/allowed to be registered, as per the decision of GNCTD.
9. Digital Integration:
9.1 GNCTD shall ensure that all implementation frameworks, including applications, approvals, verifications,
disbursements, reporting, and grievance redressal are conducted in a fully paperless manner through digital systems.
10. Institutional Framework
Nodal Departments and Responsibilities:
10.1 Transport Department
10.1.1 The Transport Department, GNCTD shall serve as the nodal department for implementation of the EV Policy
2026 and for issuing all clarifications, minor amendments and operational guidelines, if any from time to time.
10.1.2An EV Cell shall be constituted under the Special/Additional/Joint Commissioner (EV), Transport Department,
GNCTD with a dedicated hired PMC to ensure clarification, implementation and operation of EV Policy 2026.
10.2 Delhi Transco Limited (DTL) through Power Department
10.2.1 DTL through the Power Department, shall be responsible for the planning, deployment, and monitoring of all
public electric vehicle charging and battery swapping stations in the National Capital Territory of Delhi. DTL shall
ensure that public charging and swapping infrastructure remains operational and shall develop and notify service level
benchmarks for performance, uptime, and reliability of such infrastructure.
10.2.2 DTL shall also assess present and future electricity load requirements arising from EV charging demand in the
NCT of Delhi and shall ensure timely power procurement and seamless power supply through coordinated planning and
implementation with the DISCOMs.
10.3 Environment Department
10.3.1 The Environment Department shall assess and periodically quantify the emission reductions achieved through
new electric vehicle registrations under the Delhi EV Policy 2026. The Department shall develop and apply a transparent
methodology to evaluate impacts on air pollutant emissions and greenhouse gas emissions, enabling evidence-based
assessment of the environmental outcomes and overall effectiveness of the Delhi EV Policy 2026.
10.3.2 The Environment Department shall ensure strict adherence by Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and
other obligated entities to all applicable provisions of the BATTERY WASTE MANAGEMENT RULES, 2022, as
amended from time to time, including requirements related to Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), reporting, and
environmentally sound management of waste batteries.
10.4 Delhi Pollution Control Board (DPCC)
10.4.1DPCC shall, through an appropriate policy framework, facilitate the deployment of battery collection centres
across the National Capital Territory of Delhi under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, in collaboration with
authorised recyclers and other eligible entities, to enable convenient, accessible, and environmentally sound collection
of waste batteries.
10.4.2DPCC shall notify Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) and
other obligated entities to ensure the safe collection, storage, transportation, and transfer of waste batteries to authorised
recyclers or Producer Responsibility Organisations (PROs), in compliance with applicable environmental regulations,
Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) requirements, and safety standards.

10.5 Urban Local bodies (Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), Delhi Development Authority (DDA), Delhi
Cantonment Board, New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC), PWD, DUSIB, Revenue Department and other land-
owning agencies
10.5.1 On a periodic basis, the urban local bodies and other land-owning agencies shall identify suitable land parcels
for the deployment of public electric vehicle charging and battery swapping infrastructure and shall extend necessary
support to Delhi Transco Limited (DTL) for planning, approvals, and implementation of such infrastructure.
10.5.2 All new civil infrastructure projects of departments/autonomous bodies/corporations/boards and similar
institutions under GNCTD including Municipal Corporation of Delhi, New Delhi Municipal Council and Delhi
Cantonment Board shall be required to be EV-charging-ready, with adequate electrical capacity to enable the
installation of electric vehicle charging infrastructure.
10.6 Education Department
10.6.1 The Education Department, Government of NCT of Delhi, shall ensure compliance with the mandate across the
entire school bus fleet, including buses owned, leased, or hired by schools. The Department shall issue necessary
directions, integrate compliance requirements into school recognition and affiliation processes, and monitor adherence
to the mandate in coordination with Transport Department.
10.6.2 The Education Department, Government of NCT of Delhi, shall design and implement regular awareness drives
and educational campaigns in schools to sensitise students, teachers, and school management on issues related to air
pollution, its health and environmental impacts, and the measures being undertaken by the Government to improve air
quality in Delhi. The Department shall also promote student-led initiatives and practical actions to encourage sustainable
travel choices, energy conservation, and responsible environmental behaviour to support improvements in Delhi’s air
quality.
10.7District Magistrates through Revenue Department – Land Aggregation
10.7.1 The District Magistrates (DMs), through the Revenue Department, shall facilitate the identification, aggregation,
and making available of suitable land parcels for priority public infrastructure requirements, including electric vehicle
charging and swapping infrastructure and allied facilities.
11. EV Fund
11.1 A dedicated EV Fund shall be maintained under the Transport Department.
11.2 Sources of the Fund may include State Budgetary Allocations, Central and State Government Schemes and Grants,
Air Ambience Fund, Environment Compensation Charge (ECC), PM E-DRIVE Scheme, cess, taxes, and any other
approved sources.
11.3 All operational and implementation expenses subject to clause 5.1 related to the EV Policy 2026 shall be met from
the EV Fund.
11.4 Spending under EV Fund shall be as per the latest applicable delegation of financial powers rules.
12. Delhi EV Apex Committee
12.1 A Delhi EV Apex Committee, under the Chairpersonship of the Hon’ble Minister (Transport), shall be constituted
to oversee implementation of the policy, approval of the operational guidelines and management of the EV Fund.
12.2 The composition of the Committee along with ToR shall be notified separately with approval of the Hon’ble Chief
Minister.
12.3 If a cleaner fuel or technology will be available for vehicles in Delhi during the operation of the policy period, an
appropriate recommendation or suggestion regarding the same shall be made by Delhi EV Apex Committee to Council
of Ministers for decision.
13. Policy Validity
13.1 This policy shall remain in force from the date of notification till 31 March 2030, unless extended or modified by
the Government of NCT of Delhi.

5. General Provisions 
5.1. Incentives under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 shall be available only in 
respect of eligible electric vehicles purchased and registered in Delhi on or after the 
date of notification of the Policy. 
5.2. Such vehicles shall be eligible for incentives only where the corresponding vehicle 
model has been approved in accordance with these Guidelines and published on the 
designated portal of the Transport Department. 
5.3. In the event of any inconsistency between these Guidelines and the Delhi Electric 
Vehicle Policy, 2026, the provisions of the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 shall 
prevail. 
CHAPTER II - INSTITUTIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES  
6. EV Cell 
6.1. The EV Cell of the Transport Department shall be responsible for overall 
implementation and administration of these Guidelines. 
6.2. The EV Cell shall, inter alia, administer the designated portal, process registration of 
Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM), provide assistance to the Model Approval 
Committee, facilitate processing and disbursal of incentives, maintain the list of

metadata.document_title: Centralized Operating Guidelines for Delhi EV Policy 2026

page_content:
approved vehicle models and perform such other functions as may be assigned by the 
Transport Department. 
7. Model Approval Committee 
7.1. The Model Approval Committee constituted under these Guidelines shall be 
responsible for approval of vehicle models eligible for incentives under the Delhi 
Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 in accordance with the provisions of these Guidelines. 
8. District Transport Officers 
8.1. The District Transport Officers (DTO) shall verify applications for purchase 
incentives and scrapping incentives in accordance with these Guidelines. 
8.2. The DTOs shall communicate deficiencies, where applicable, process eligible 
applications and recommend disbursal of incentives in accordance with the timelines 
prescribed under these Guidelines. 
9. Delhi Transco Limited 
9.1. Delhi Transco Limited (DTL), being the State Nodal Agency for development of 
charging infrastructure under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026, shall prepare a 
detailed action plan and operational guidelines for establishment of charging 
infrastructure in consultation with the Distribution Licensees (DISCOMs) and other 
concerned stakeholders. 
CHAPTER III - ELIGIBILITY OF VEHICLE MODELS 
10. Eligible Vehicle Models 
10.1. Purchase incentives under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 shall be available 
only in respect of vehicle models eligible under this Chapter and approved in 
accordance with these Guidelines. 
10.2. The technical eligibility criteria and localisation requirements prescribed in Annexure 
II have been adopted by the Government of NCT of Delhi for the purposes of 
implementation of the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026. The technical eligibility 
criteria and localisation requirements for Electric Two Wheelers and Electric Three 
Wheeler Passenger Vehicles are based on the applicable provisions of the PM E 
DRIVE Scheme. The technical eligibility criteria and localisation requirements for 
Electric N1 category vehicles are based on the applicable provisions of the FAME 
India Scheme Phase II. These shall form the basis for determining the eligibility of 
vehicle models under these Guidelines. 
10.3. The following vehicle models shall be deemed to have been approved under the Delhi 
Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026:

metadata.document_title: Centralized Operating Guidelines for Delhi EV Policy 2026

page_content:
10.3.1. Electric Two Wheeler vehicle models included in the active list of models 
approved under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme as on 31 July 2026, or approved under 
the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto 
Components, shall be deemed to have been approved under these Guidelines and 
shall remain eligible for incentives under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 
until 31 July 2027. 
10.3.2. Electric Three Wheeler models approved under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme during 
the period from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, or approved under the 
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto 
Components, shall be deemed to have been approved under these Guidelines and 
shall remain eligible for incentives under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 
until 31 March 2027. 
10.3.3. Electric N1 category vehicle models approved under the Production Linked 
Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components shall be deemed 
to have been approved under these Guidelines and shall be eligible for incentives 
under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026. 
10.4. Vehicle models not covered under Clause 10.3 shall be considered for approval under 
these Guidelines, provided they satisfy the technical and localisation requirements 
prescribed in Annexure II. 
CHAPTER IV - MODEL APPROV AL COMMITTEE 
11. Constitution of the Model Approval Committee 
11.1. A Model Approval Committee is hereby constituted for approval of vehicle models 
under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 and shall consist of the following 
members: 
11.1.1. Chairperson - Special Commissioner (Electric Vehicles), Transport Department; 
11.1.2. Member – Joint/Deputy Commissioner (Electric Vehicles), Transport 
Department; 
11.1.3. Member – Joint/Deputy Commissioner (Operations), Transport Department; and, 
11.1.4. Member - One expert from a panel of experts drawn from testing agencies 
notified under Rule 126 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989.  
11.1.4.1. The Transport Department shall maintain a panel of experts nominated 
by testing agencies notified under Rule 126 of the Central Motor 
Vehicles Rules, 1989. 
12. Functions of the Model Approval Committee

metadata.document_title: Centralized Operating Guidelines for Delhi EV Policy 2026

page_content:
12.1. The Model Approval Committee shall: 
12.1.1. consider applications for approval of vehicle models submitted under these 
Guidelines; 
12.1.2. verify compliance of vehicle models with the eligibility conditions and the 
technical and localisation requirements prescribed under these Guidelines in 
Annexure II; 
12.1.3. consider applications for approval of vehicle models not covered under the 
deemed approval provisions contained in Chapter III; 
12.1.4. seek such clarifications or additional information from the OEM as may be 
necessary for verification of compliance with these Guidelines; 
12.1.5. approve eligible vehicle models for inclusion in the list of approved vehicle 
models maintained on the designated portal; and  
12.1.6. perform such other functions as may be assigned by the Transport Department 
consistent with the provisions of the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026. 
12.2. The Model Approval Committee shall approve or reject an application solely on the 
basis of compliance with the eligibility conditions, technical and localisation 
requirements prescribed under Annexure II of these Guidelines. 
13. Decisions of the Model Approval Committee 
13.1. Upon receipt of an application for approval of a vehicle model, the Model Approval 
Committee shall examine the application and, within seven (7) working days, either: 
13.1.1. approve the application; or 
13.1.2. communicate the deficiencies, if any, to the concerned OEM through the 
designated portal 
13.2. Where deficiencies are communicated under Clause 13.1.2, the concerned OEM shall 
rectify such deficiencies and submit the required information or documents through 
the designated portal within seven (7) working days from the date of such 
communication. 
13.3. Upon receipt of the information or documents submitted under Clause 13.2, the 
Model Approval Committee shall communicate its final decision to approve or reject 
the application through the designated portal within seven (7) working days.
  
13.4. The EV Cell shall publish and maintain on the designated portal an updated list of 
vehicle models approved under these Guidelines, including such particulars as may be 
necessary for implementation of the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026.

CHAPTER V - REGISTRATION OF OEM AND VEHICLE MODEL 
APPROV AL 
14. Registration of OEM  
14.1. Every OEM seeking approval of vehicle models under the Delhi Electric Vehicle 
Policy, 2026 shall register and submit an application along with the documents on the 
designated portal in the manner specified in Annexure I. 
14.2. Upon verification of the application and supporting documents, the EV Cell shall 
register the OEM and provide access to the designated portal. 
15. Application for Approval of Vehicle Models by OEM 
15.1. A registered OEM shall apply for approval of one or more vehicle models through the 
designated portal in the prescribed format accompanied with the documents specified 
in Annexure III. 
15.2. Vehicle models deemed to have been approved under Chapter III shall not be required 
to undergo the model approval process prescribed under this Chapter. The concerned 
OEM shall complete registration in accordance with Annexure I and furnish the 
prescribed company and authorised dealer details to enable mapping of the OEM and 
its authorised dealers with the deemed approved vehicle models on the designated 
portal for implementation of the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026. 
15.3. Vehicle models not covered under the deemed approval provisions of Chapter III shall 
be considered by the Model Approval Committee in accordance with these 
Guidelines. 
15.4. The Model Approval Committee may seek such clarifications or additional 
information from the OEM as may be necessary for verification of compliance with 
these Guidelines. 
16. Responsibilities of Original Equipment Manufacturers and Authorised 
Dealers 
16.1. Every OEM shall ensure that only vehicle models approved under these Guidelines 
and published on the designated portal are represented as eligible for incentives under 
the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026. 
16.2. Every OEM shall promptly inform the Transport Department of any modification 
affecting the technical specifications, localisation requirements or eligibility of an

metadata.document_title: Centralized Operating Guidelines for Delhi EV Policy 2026

page_content:
approved vehicle model and obtain fresh approval before representing such model as 
eligible for incentives under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026. 
16.3. Every authorised dealer shall, at the time of booking of an eligible electric 
vehicle, inform the purchaser in writing whether the vehicle model is eligible for 
incentives under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 and furnish the 
declaration in the format specified in Annexure VIII. 
16.4. The OEM and its authorised dealers shall be jointly responsible for the correctness 
and authenticity of information furnished in connection with vehicle model approval 
under these Guidelines. 
16.5. All OEMs operating in the National Capital Territory of Delhi shall ensure 
deployment of at least one public electric vehicle charging station at each authorised 
dealership, comprising a minimum of three (3) charging points for two and three 
wheelers and two (2) charging points for four wheelers, in accordance with the Delhi 
Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026, within six (6) months from the date of notification of 
these Guidelines. 
16.6. Where an authorised dealership fails to comply with this requirement within the 
prescribed period, the Transport Department may deactivate the dealership from the 
designated portal for processing incentive applications under the Delhi Electric 
Vehicle Policy, 2026 until such time as the charging infrastructure requirement is 
complied with. 
CHAPTER VI - PURCHASE INCENTIVES 
17. Submission of Application 
17.1. Eligible applicants seeking purchase incentives under the Delhi Electric Vehicle 
Policy, 2026 shall submit an application through the designated portal within thirty 
(30) days from the date of generation of the Registration Certificate (RC). 
17.2. Individual applicants shall be eligible to apply for purchase incentives only in respect 
of vehicles purchased and registered in Delhi, are in their name and subject to 
fulfilment of the residency and other eligibility conditions prescribed under Annexure 
IX. 
17.3. Companies, firms and other eligible entities shall be eligible to apply for purchase 
incentives in respect of vehicles purchased and registered in Delhi, are in their name, 
subject to fulfilment of the eligibility conditions prescribed under Annexure X, 
including proof that the registered office of the applicant is situated in the National 
Capital Territory of Delhi. 
18. Scrutiny and Verification

page_content:
18.1. Upon receipt of an application, the concerned DTO shall verify the application and 
supporting documents in accordance with the provisions of Annexure XII of these 
Guidelines. 
18.2. Where the DTO finds that the application is incomplete or requires clarification, the 
deficiencies shall be communicated to the applicant through the designated portal 
within fifteen (15) working days from the date of receipt of the application. 
18.3. The applicant shall rectify the deficiencies and submit the required information or 
documents within seven (7) working days from the date of communication of such 
deficiencies. 
18.4. Upon receipt of a complete application or the information furnished under Clause 
18.3, the DTO shall complete the verification and communicate the decision on the 
application within seven (7) working days. 
19. Approval and Disbursal 
19.1. Upon being satisfied that the applicant fulfils the eligibility conditions prescribed 
under Annexure XII of these Guidelines, the DTO shall approve the application for 
disbursal of the purchase incentive. 
19.2. Purchase incentives for individual applicants shall be disbursed through the Aadhaar 
Based Payment System (ABPS). 
19.3. Purchase incentives for companies, firms and other eligible entities shall be disbursed 
to the verified bank account furnished by the applicant. 
19.4. The eligible subsidy amount shall be disbursed within sixty (60) days from the date of 
submission of the application on the designated portal, subject to verification and 
fulfilment of the applicable requirements under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 
2026 and these Guidelines. 
19.5. The status of the application, including any deficiencies, approval, rejection or 
disbursal of incentive, shall be communicated to the applicant through the designated 
portal and through SMS alerts on the registered mobile number of the applicant. 
19.6. Rejection of an application shall not preclude an applicant from submitting a fresh 
application, provided such application is otherwise eligible under the Delhi Electric 
Vehicle Policy, 2026 and these Guidelines. 
CHAPTER VII - SCRAPPING INCENTIVES 
20. Eligibility for Scrapping Incentives 
20.1. Scrapping incentives shall be available only in respect of vehicles and applicants 
fulfilling the eligibility conditions prescribed under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 
2026.

metadata.document_title: Centralized Operating Guidelines for Delhi EV Policy 2026

page_content:
20.2. The applicant shall purchase a new eligible electric vehicle within six (6) months 
from the date of issuance of the Certificate of Deposit (CoD) by an Authorised 
Vehicle Scrapping Facility, wherever applicable under the Policy. 
20.3. The scrapping incentive shall be available only to the owner of the scrapped vehicle in 
whose favour the Certificate of Deposit (CoD) has been issued. 
21. Submission of Application 
21.1. Applicants shall submit an application for scrapping incentive through the designated 
portal, accompanied by the Certificate of Deposit (CoD) and the documents 
prescribed under these Guidelines. 
21.2. Individual applicants shall be eligible to claim scrapping incentives only in respect of 
vehicle categories covered under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026, subject to 
fulfilment of the residency and other eligibility conditions prescribed under Annexure 
XI. 
21.3. Companies, firms and other entities shall be eligible to claim scrapping incentives in 
respect of vehicles registered in their name, subject to fulfilment of the eligibility 
conditions prescribed under Annexure XI, including proof that the registered office of 
the applicant is situated in the National Capital Territory of Delhi. 
22. Verification and Disbursal 
22.1. Upon receipt of an application, the concerned DTO shall scrutinise and verify the 
application and supporting documents in accordance with Annexure XII. 
22.2. Where the application is incomplete or requires clarification, the deficiencies shall be 
communicated to the applicant through the designated portal within fifteen (15) 
working days from the date of receipt of the application. 
22.3. The applicant shall rectify the deficiencies and submit the required information or 
documents within seven (7) working days from the date of communication of such 
deficiencies. 
22.4. Upon receipt of a complete application or the information furnished under Clause 
22.3, the DTO shall complete the verification and communicate the decision on the 
application within seven (7) working days. 
22.5. The scrapping incentive shall be disbursed within the timeline prescribed under the 
Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026, subject to verification and fulfilment of the 
applicable requirements. 
22.6. The status of the application, including any deficiencies, approval, rejection or 
disbursal of incentive, shall be communicated to the applicant through the designated 
portal and through SMS alerts on the registered mobile number of the applicant.

metadata.document_title: Centralized Operating Guidelines for Delhi EV Policy 2026

page_content:
22.7. Rejection of an application shall not preclude an applicant from submitting a fresh 
application, provided such application is otherwise eligible under the Delhi Electric 
Vehicle Policy, 2026 and these Guidelines. 
CHAPTER VIII - GRIEV ANCE REDRESSAL 
23. Grievance Redressal
 
23.1. Any applicant aggrieved by issues relating to registration on the designated portal, 
submission of an application, verification of documents, processing or disbursal of 
incentives, or any other matter relating to implementation of the Delhi Electric 
Vehicle Policy, 2026, and these Guidelines may submit a grievance by email at 
evpolicy2026@gmail.com or through the dedicated helpline notified by the Transport 
Department and displayed on the designated portal. 
23.2. The EV Cell shall be the nodal authority for receipt, examination and disposal of 
grievances received under these Guidelines. 
23.3. Every grievance shall be acknowledged within three (3) working days of its receipt. 
23.4. The EV Cell shall examine the grievance and dispose of the same within seven (7) 
working days from the date of receipt of the grievance. 
23.5. Where additional information or documents are required for disposal of the grievance, 
the EV Cell may seek the same from the applicant. The applicant shall furnish the 
required information or documents within seven (7) working days from the date of 
such communication. The period taken by the applicant to furnish the additional 
information or documents shall not be counted for the purpose of computing the 
timeline specified under Clause 23.4. 
23.6. Any grievance remaining unresolved beyond the prescribed timeline shall be placed 
before the Joint Commissioner (Electric Vehicles) for appropriate directions. 
23.7. The decision on the grievance shall be communicated to the applicant through the 
email address from which the grievance was received. The applicant may also be 
informed through a helpline on the registered mobile number, wherever available. 
CHAPTER IX - MISCELLANEOUS 
24. Operationalisation of No Entry Exemption for Electric N2 Category 
Goods Vehicles 
24.1. The Transport Department shall implement the provisions relating to exemption from 
no entry restrictions under the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026 through the 
designated portal, which shall be integrated with the V AHAN database and such other 
enforcement systems, databases and digital platforms as may be notified by the 
Transport Department. Eligible vehicles shall be identified based on the date of

metadata.document_title: Centralized Operating Guidelines for Delhi EV Policy 2026

page_content:
registration of the vehicle in the National Capital Territory of Delhi as recorded in the 
V AHAN database. 
24.2. The Transport Department shall prepare and maintain, through the designated portal, a 
real time list of vehicles eligible for exemption under this Chapter. The designated 
portal shall also display the number of vehicles granted exemption under the Delhi 
Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026. 
24.3. The list of eligible vehicles shall be closed upon registration of one thousand (1,000) 
eligible vehicles or on completion of three (3) months from the date of notification of 
the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026, whichever is earlier, unless otherwise decided 
by the Delhi EV Apex Committee. 
24.4. The Transport Department shall integrate the details of vehicles granted exemption 
under this clause with the relevant enforcement systems, databases and digital 
platforms to facilitate implementation and enforcement of the exemption from no 
entry restrictions. 
24.5. The Transport Department shall notify a separate registration series for Electric N2 
category goods vehicles granted exemption from no entry restrictions under the Delhi 
Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026.  
24.6. Where it is subsequently found that a vehicle has been granted exemption on the basis 
of false information, misrepresentation or is otherwise found to be ineligible under the 
Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026, the Transport Department may withdraw the 
exemption after giving the registered owner a reasonable opportunity of being heard. 
25. Validity and Continuity of the Guidelines 
25.1. Any amendment, or modification to these Guidelines shall be carried out with the 
approval of the Delhi EV Apex Committee constituted under the Delhi Electric 
Vehicle Policy, 2026. 
25.2. These Guidelines shall remain in force during the validity of the Delhi Electric 
Vehicle Policy, 2026 and any extension thereof, unless modified or superseded by the 
Government of NCT of Delhi. 
25.3. Applications received, vehicle models approved and incentives disbursed under these 
Guidelines shall continue to remain valid unless specifically reviewed or withdrawn 
by the Transport Department.

ANNEXURE II 
TECHNICAL ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA FOR APPROV AL OF VEHICLE MODELS 
BY THE MODEL APPROV AL COMMITTEE 
1. Applicability 
1.1. This Annexure shall apply only to vehicle models requiring approval by the Model 
Approval Committee under Chapter IV of these Guidelines. 
1.2. Vehicle models deemed approved under Chapter III shall not require assessment 
under this Annexure. 
2. General Requirements 
2.1. The technical eligibility criteria and localisation requirements prescribed in this 
Annexure have been adopted from the applicable technical eligibility criteria under 
the PM E DRIVE Scheme for Electric Two Wheelers and Electric Three Wheeler 
Passenger Vehicles, the FAME India Scheme Phase II for Electric N1 category 
vehicles, and the applicable localisation requirements under the Phased 
Manufacturing Programme (PMP) and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme 
for Automobile and Auto Components. 
2.2. Unless otherwise provided in these Guidelines, every vehicle model seeking approval 
under this Annexure shall: 
2.2.1. be manufactured in India; 
2.2.2. comply with the applicable localisation requirements under the Phased 
Manufacturing Programme (PMP), as adopted by the Government of NCT 
of Delhi from time to time; 
2.2.3. comply with the applicable provisions of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 
1989, including those relating to type approval, classification, categorisation, 
road worthiness and registration; 
2.2.4. possess a valid Type Approval Certificate issued by a testing agency notified 
under Rule 126 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989; and 
2.2.5. vehicle model shall comply with the applicable Automotive Industry 
Standards (AIS) and all applicable provisions of the Central Motor Vehicles 
Rules, 1989. 
2.2.6. be accompanied by the minimum manufacturer warranty prescribed under 
this Annexure and maintain adequate after sales service facilities for the life 
of the vehicle.

together with any additional information sought by the Model Approval

scheme or revised technical eligibility criteria or localisation requirements applicable
to any vehicle category covered under this Annexure, the Delhi EV Apex Committee
may review and adopt such provisions, in whole or in part, for the purposes of these
Guidelines. Upon such adoption, the relevant provisions of this Annexure shall apply
from the date notified by the Transport Department.
